original_question: Let S = P^2 and let I = (y, x^r)^m with integers r > 9 and m >= 1. If Y is a general element of the Hilbert-scheme locus Hilb_I S associated to this monomial ideal, is it true that H^0(I_Y tensor O_{P^2}(d)) = 0 for every degree d satisfying d <= m sqrt(r)?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 2.4.4 in Section 2.4, "Regularity for generic monomial zero-schemes": the vanishing statement for S = P^2 and I = (y, x^r)^m with r > 9, for general Y in Hilb_I^S and all d <= m sqrt(r). Your draft is aiming at this narrower vanishing conjecture, not the stronger expected-dimension formula in Conjecture 2.4.3. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
correct_elements: You already have the correct surface S = P^2, the correct special monomial ideal I = (y, x^r)^m, the condition r > 9, the right parameter space Hilb_I^S, the "general Y" quantifier, and the exact vanishing range d <= m sqrt(r). That matches Conjecture 2.4.4 essentially verbatim. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
missing_details: The paper first fixes a field k and views I as a monomial ideal in k[x,y]; S is a smooth projective surface over k, and in this conjecture S = P^2_k. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

One should define Z = Spec(k[x,y]/I) and n = dim_k(k[x,y]/I); Hilb_I^S is then the irreducible constructible subset of Hilb^n(S) whose closed points correspond to subschemes Y subset S isomorphic to Z. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
I_Y should be identified as the ideal sheaf of the subscheme Y subset S. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The paper phrases the twist by a divisor D on S; for S = P^2 one may write D = dH, with H the class of a line, so O_S(D) = O_{P^2}(d). ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The variable d should be understood as an integer divisor degree; otherwise the expression O_{P^2}(d) is not defined. The paper's range is "for all d <= m sqrt(r)", and negative d are trivial cases because H^0(O_{P^2}(d)) = 0. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
The question is conjectural in the paper, not stated as a theorem or proved equivalence. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The nearby context explains the motivation: I = (y, x^r)^m is a specialization/collision of r distinct m-fold points, and this is why the conjecture is linked to Nagata and SHGH. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
refined_question: Let k be a field, let S = P^2_k, let I = (y, x^r)^m be the monomial ideal in k[x,y] with natural numbers r,m and r > 9, and let Z = Spec(k[x,y]/I). Write n = dim_k(k[x,y]/I), and let Hilb_I^S be the irreducible constructible subset of Hilb^n(S) whose closed points parameterize subschemes Y subset S isomorphic to Z. If Y is a general member of Hilb_I^S and H is the hyperplane class on S, is it true that for every integer d with d <= m sqrt(r) one has H^0(S, I_Y ⊗ O_S(dH)) = 0? ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly matches Section 2.4, not the paper's earlier problems: the exact tuple S = P^2, I = (y, x^r)^m, r > 9, general Y in Hilb_I^S, and the vanishing range d <= m sqrt(r) is precisely Conjecture 2.4.4. The surrounding lines in Section 2.4 supply the missing stand-alone definitions of Z, n, Hilb_I^S, and I_Y, and explain that this conjecture is motivated by viewing (y, x^r)^m as a collision of r distinct m-fold points; the authors then state that Conjecture 2.4.4 implies Nagata's conjecture and is implied by the stronger Conjecture 2.4.3. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
